To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the isothermal oxygen permeability flux through sintered disks of BE25 is rate controlled by solid state diffusion and surface oxygen exchange, the oxygen exchange rate is 1.2 × 10−5 mol cm−2 s−1 at 700°C, the oxygen ionic transference numbers are close to unity, and the oxygen ionic conductivity is 1.5 × 10−3 Ω−1 cm−1 at 750°C.

BE25 exhibits a high oxygen semi-permeability flux at high temperatures and that it is possible to control the rate limiting step in the oxygen semi-permeation process by the choice of the oxygen partial pressure.

the oxygen permeation flux through a BE25 membrane can be described by an equation that contains two rate limiting parameters, one for the surface exchange rate and one for the solid state diffusion of oxygen.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the oxygen semiper-meability of BE25.
the development of a new type of ceramic membrane for oxygen separation and oxygen enrichment of air, and for the production of oxygen from air at low temperatures.
the development of new ceramic membranes for oxygen separation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

BE25 behaves as a solid oxide ion conductor with a p-type electronic conductivity, which is rate limiting in oxygen permeation under the applied conditions, and that this behaviour is consistent with a surface oxygen exchange reaction that is rate limiting for the oxygen semipermetation flux in the presence of a gas phase oxygen partial pressure gradient.
BE25 is an excellent solid electrolyte for the separation of oxygen from air at elevated temperatures.
the oxygen permeability of BE25 can be described by an equation of the form J=J1+J2 where J1 is the flux limited by solid state diffusion and J2 by surface oxygen exchange.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the oxygen semiconductivity and the oxygen semiper-meability of erbia stabilized bismuth oxide are well understood and that BE25 is an ideal material for the construction of oxygen semipermeable membranes.
the oxygen semiconductivity of BE25 is not high enough to allow for the application of the material as a solid electrolyte in oxygen separation membranes.
BE25 is a promising candidate for oxygen separation membranes, though further improvement in its oxygen semipermeation flux and stability at elevated temperature are required.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the oxygen permeability of BE25 can be described with a single parameter, the hole diffusion coefficient.
the surface exchange reaction can be rate limiting in oxygen semipermeation in case of p-type solid electrolytes.
the oxygen semiconductivity of BE25, which is the basis for its oxygen semi-permeability, can be evaluated from oxygen semi-permeation measurements.
